name: Gas engine generator set
summary: A spark-ignited reciprocating engine on natural gas, biogas or LPG driving an alternator, shown as a generating source.
description: A gas engine generator set uses a spark-ignited reciprocating engine running on natural gas, biogas, landfill gas or LPG. These sets are common in combined heat and power plants, prime power microgrids and sites with a reliable gas supply, and they are often run continuously rather than only as backup.

Single-line diagrams draw the alternator circle with an engine block marked G or GAS, the generator breaker, and sometimes heat recovery references. When several sets run in parallel, a common synchronising bus and a load-sharing controller appear alongside.

Gas engines usually accept large load steps less readily than diesel engines, which affects how a microgrid sequences load after a blackout. The symbol does not express block-load acceptance, gas pressure requirements or emissions limits.
readingNotes: Check the load-step limits in the controller documents before assuming the set can pick up a whole bus at once.
Heat recovery or CHP notes indicate continuous running.
drawingChecklist: State fuel type and rating basis.
Reference load acceptance and start sequence.
distinction: A gas engine set uses spark ignition and gaseous fuel; a gas turbine generator uses a continuous-combustion turbine.
